summary: RomM is a self-hosted ROM manager designed to help you organise, enrich, and play retro games across hundreds of different platforms. It acts as a centralised control panel for large collections of game files, streamlining metadata management and browser-based access.
goodFor: It is a good fit for self-hosters with extensive retro game libraries who want a web-accessible interface to catalogue and play titles.
watchOut: The software is distributed under the AGPL-3.0 licence, which imposes strict copyleft obligations if you modify and network-host the code. Additionally, relying on browser-based emulation for hundreds of disparate platforms can introduce complex performance and compatibility trade-offs.
deployNotes: As a containerised application, you will typically need to configure persistent volumes for your game library and metadata storage, along with a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
